description: A REAL three-segment HS256 JWT (header.payload.signature) and its real alg:none tamper twin, for the identity / web-app / api-paradigms PEEL legs. The jwt-7519 parser base64url-splits the segments and JSON-decodes header+payload; the decode IS the oracle (no key needed — proving encoding != protection). HS256 verification delegates to crypto-transform (HMAC-SHA-256).

provenance.captured_with: node:crypto: HMAC-SHA-256 over base64url(header).base64url(payload) with a fixed secret; segments base64url-encoded per RFC 7515 §2
provenance.cross_checked_against: python base64.urlsafe_b64decode of each segment; the signature recomputes identically (HS256_VERIFIES=true). Decoded header={alg:HS256,typ:JWT}; payload carries iss/sub/aud/iat/exp.
provenance.honesty_note: Real RFC 7519 token. The decode is the parser's output over the real base64url bytes. The alg:none twin is a real tampered instance (header alg swapped to 'none', signature segment emptied) — the genuine attack, not a mock. The exp (1718203600 = 2024-06-12T14:46:40Z) is genuinely in the past, so this also serves as a real expired-token leg.
provenance.secret_note: The HMAC secret 'grc-bootcamp-shared-hs256-secret' is published here ONLY so the HS256 leg is reproducible; in the lab the learner verifies the signature by recomputing the HMAC, not by reading a key.

algnone_twin.attack: alg:none — the unprotected-token attack (RFC 8725 §2.1). The signature segment is empty; an alg:none verifier would accept it as valid.
